messages.content: Can you help me Get object descriptors related to a domain example.org on VirusTotal? The relationship I want to check is subdomains. You should just return the related object's IDs (and context attributes, if any) instead of returning all attributes. My key is my_api. Set the limit to 10 and the continuation cursor to abc.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to use the VirusTotal API to get object descriptors related to a domain example.org with relationship subdomains. They want only the related object's IDs and context attributes, not all attributes. Provide the request body JSON. The user also says "My key is my_api". So we need to produce a JSON request body that includes the key, limit, cursor, etc.

We have to respond with the request body JSON. According to instructions: "When responding to a user request, you should just return the request body JSON." So we output the JSON body that would be sent to the API endpoint. We don't actually call the API. So we produce something like:

{
  "key": "my_api",
  "limit": 10,
  "cursor": "abc",
  "relationship_type": "subdomains",
  "object_id": "example.org"
}

But we need to confirm the correct field names. For VirusTotal API v3, the endpoint for retrieving related objects is GET /objects/{id}/relationships?relationship_type=subdomains&limit=10&cursor=abc. But the request body might include key, limit, cursor, relationship_type, object_id. The user specifically says "Set the limit to 10 and the continuation cursor to abc." So we include those fields. Also they want only the related object's IDs and context attributes. That might be a parameter like "fields=id,context_attributes" or "include_fields=id,context_attributes". In VT API v3, there is an optional query param "fields" to specify which fields to return. But the user wants only IDs and context attributes. So we can set "fields=id,context_attributes". But the instruction says "just return the related object's IDs (and context attributes, if any) instead of returning all attributes." So we need to include that in the request body. So we add "fields": ["id","context_attributes"] maybe. Or "fields": "id,context_attributes".

Thus the request body JSON could be:

{
  "key": "my_api",
  "limit": 10,
  "cursor": "abc",
  "relationship_type": "subdomains",
  "object_id": "example.org",
  "fields": ["id","context_attributes"]
}

Alternatively, "fields": "id,context_attributes". Let's choose array form.

Also note that the user didn't mention the API version. We'll assume v3. The request body may not require "object_id" but "id" field. But we can include "object_id" as per the description. The user said "Get object descriptors related to a domain example.org on VirusTotal". So we need to provide the ID of the domain. Domain ID might be "domain/example.org". But we can just put "example.org" as the ID. The user didn't ask for the full ID format. So we can just put "example.org".

Thus final JSON:

{
  "key": "my_api",
  "limit": 10,
  "cursor": "abc",
  "relationship_type": "subdomains",
  "object_id": "example.org",
  "fields": ["id","context_attributes"]
}

We should output this JSON exactly.
